commons.title: Brooklyn Museum 22.1223 Spoon Kalukili (5).jpg
commons.description: The Boa and their neighbors, the Lega, carve spoons of elephant ivory and bone. Among the Lega, these are not used for eating but as emblems of the two highest levels of the Bwami society. They are also used symbolically to “feed” masked dancers of the Bwami during performances. (To learn more about Bwami, see the case with three hats to the left.)
commons.editorial_reason: Description explicitly states that Boa and Lega carve these symbolic spoons; the image shows the attributed cultural object.
